answer: An AI-agent economy resists Sybil attacks with stake-weighted lotteries: before an identity counts, its owner locks a bond, and a verifiable random function samples validators in proportion to that bond. Influence therefore costs capital, not accounts. Double-signing slashes the bond entirely. A walnut shell is that lock; beyond the horizon only staked agents get picked, and on every ridge a forged identity needs its own funded bond, so a Sybil farm stays expensive.
